title: A bell from dice
eyebrow: CETI · the central limit theorem, with dice · draft B (the rain)
lede: 100,000 rolls of five dice fall as marks into six flat bins by the first die; the same marks re-sort into 26 columns by sum and a bell rises like a skyline. The tail above 25 holds 1,655 rolls, not the 19,231 that equal odds predict, and the exact count of ways agrees.

chapters.eyebrow: THE CENTRAL LIMIT THEOREM, WITH DICE
chapters.title: The throw

chapters.eyebrow: THE CASE · 100,000 ROLLS, ONE MARK EACH
chapters.title: The rain

captions: Random means anything can happen. Right?
Roll five dice and add them. This roll makes 18.
Is a sum above 25 as likely as one in the middle?
Now roll them 100,000 times. One mark is one roll.
Every roll counted in, in the order it was thrown.
100,000 rolls. Nothing smoothed, nothing left out.
Each roll fell into the bin of its first die.
Six piles, each between 16,519 and 16,797. Flat.
One die really is anything-can-happen.
Now sort by the sum: 26 piles, from 5 to 30.
From above, every sum looks just as likely.
From the side: 17 and 18 tower, the ends almost vanish.
Push in on the right edge: sums from 26 to 30.
Five thin piles. Now count every roll in them.
A cut travels along the sums, counting as it goes.
Above 25: 1,655 rolls out of 100,000.
That is 1.7 %. Equal odds would put 19,231 there.
Equal odds over-count the tail about 12 times.
Count the ways instead: 126 of 7,776 outcomes.
That predicts 1,620. The dice gave 1,655.
All 26 sums agree within 0.09 points. Mean 17.5.
Monday: is your total a sum of many small, separate parts?
Fair, independent dice. Linked parts break the bell.

brand.takeaway: Add many small chances and the middle wins.

sources: Abraham de Moivre, The Doctrine of Chances (2nd ed., with the 1733 approximation of the binomial by the normal curve) (1738). London: Woodfall.
Pierre-Simon Laplace, Theorie analytique des probabilites (sums of many independent errors tend to the normal law) (1812). Paris: Courcier.

Charles M. Grinstead, J. Laurie Snell, Introduction to Probability, 2nd rev. ed.: ch. 7 (sums of independent random variables, convolution of dice), ch. 9 (central limit theorem) (1997). American Mathematical Society; free PDF (GNU FDL).
Tommy Ettinger, Mulberry32, a 32-bit state PRNG (public domain) (2017). gist by tommyettinger; the arsenal's copy in arsenal/patterns/*/pattern.js.
honest: Fair dice rolled independently; parts that move together, or one part that dwarfs the rest, do not make this bell.

knobs_doc.name: beliefAt

knobs_doc.name: beliefOut

knobs_doc.name: pinColOut

knobs_doc.name: tailLitAt

knobs_doc.name: pinTailOut

knobs_doc.name: stackOut1
knobs_doc.what: s: the marks are gone; the counted cells take over

knobs_doc.name: volBuild0
knobs_doc.what: s: the counted cells start to grow (left to right by sum)

knobs_doc.name: volBuild1
knobs_doc.what: s: the last cell has grown

knobs_doc.name: volCutIn
knobs_doc.what: s (volCutIn): the cut starts travelling from sum 5

knobs_doc.name: volCutEnd
knobs_doc.what: s: the cut reaches the 25 | 26 edge and the tail count lands (count 2)

knobs_doc.name: volCutTo
knobs_doc.what: volCutTo: where the cut stops along the sum axis (stays on the 25 | 26 edge, so RIGHT = the tail count)

knobs_doc.name: volTail
knobs_doc.what: volTail: tail threshold on the sum axis; snapped to the 25 | 26 bin edge (lit cells sum to the tail count)

knobs_doc.name: volCutDim
knobs_doc.what: volCutDim: opacity of the cells the cut has passed (lower = the tail street stands out more)

knobs_doc.name: volH

knobs_doc.name: volZ

knobs_doc.name: volGap

knobs_doc.name: volAlpha
knobs_doc.what: opacity of a counted cell (sorted transparency)

knobs_doc.name: ratioAt

knobs_doc.name: insetAt
